decisions.why: Round 1's ground ('neither ruling orders a tool') was read off a bundle missing tooling_fix and is withdrawn. rulings.md now carries the second ruling's tooling_fix verbatim: 'make the earlier ruling's cap ... the standing rule: when a unit's second review FAILs on BREVITY alone and FIDELITY passes, the text as reviewed stands and its PASS is recorded automatically, with no arbiter ask.' The arbiter ordered the standing rule; its merit is not this review's to weigh. A caller-typed verdict delivers 'recorded automatically'; 'brevity alone, FIDELITY passing' is the caller's reading of the reply, as every recorded verdict is, so it is no weaker enforcement than the record already has; the by cell names the ruling. The reach of its 'second' test is ruled separately, D6c.

decisions.summary: The tool counts a review as a SECOND when 'a FAIL of the same guard and kind must stand in the record, its wording superseded'; otherwise it refuses it as a first review's.
decisions.why: The ruling's standing rule is for 'a unit's second review'. Guard and kind do not identify a unit: the block's own ranking puts family 1 (cut after a FAIL) and family 10 (never reviewed) both under make_only_hooks refuse, finished_run_hooks refuse holds 4 keys and set_down_hooks refuse 2. On the block's words, while any superseded FAIL of a guard and kind stands, a FIRST review of a sibling wording of that guard and kind that fails on brevity is recorded PASS, the text standing - a rewrite of a reviewer's FAIL into a PASS that no ruling ordered, reaching past the ordered rule (a guard that rewrites work is in scope only for exactly what was ordered). The deletion of superseded rows at T177's end narrows the window but does not close it: any future round that cuts one wording of a guard and kind and reviews a sibling before cleanup falls in it, and the block's method reviews wordings in parallel. None of the three grounds holds: tying the test to the unit is not impossible (each unit already carries the full text it replaced, and the by cell already names 'the first: <agent>'), the ruling does not imply the wider test, and the literal rule defeats nothing. Ruled on the block's text without reading the code. CURE: tie the prior FAIL to the wording this text replaced - e.g. the caller names the superseded key, and the tool checks that key's row is a FAIL of the same guard and kind, superseded by this one, recording that key in the by cell - and say so in the block. If the code already ties it so, restate the block's sentence to say so and this decision is within.

decisions.summary: make arbiter-fix-done gains LANDING=<task> FILES= [F=]: checks the fix is done with its test, its files and test committed in the clone, and the task an open task of F; writes no done row but keeps the fix pending in the clone's git dir (arbiter-fix-landing.json); make land writes each pending fix's done row into its home's arbiter.jsonl in the tick commit and forgets the entry once the push lands
decisions.why: A process fix to the landings, found in this feature's own T177 landing (three commits and a refused landing where one would do); FR-013 counts work that makes the landings faster as performance work, the request asks for efficiency and process improvements and that performance work come first, and the plan's measured before row shows the defect. It adds a route and narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: DECISION: the done rows are written BEFORE the ticks, not after as the handoff drafted, because the closing check at a feature's last tick reads open fixes
decisions.why: An ordering inside the new route chosen so the route works for a landing that closes its feature; writing after would leave that case refused. It makes the route reach every landing rather than fewer.

decisions.summary: The land's first pass reads its tasks' hold with the fixes pending on those tasks left out (fix_hold_landing via Ask.landing); a plain make tick is still held
decisions.why: Feature 379's hold (a fix holds the tick until settled) keeps its purpose: the fix's done row and the tick go out in one commit and one push, or neither does (refused tick undoes the logs, failed push's revert removes the rows). The hold is lifted only for a fix this landing itself settles; every other tick is held as before.

decisions.summary: A refused tick puts the logs back (Settled::undo) and a failed push's revert takes the rows out; the fix stays pending either way
decisions.why: Keeps the append-only log and the 379 hold honest on failure; no request clause is narrowed.

decisions.summary: ENGINE=1 (settled a fix committed in the clone at once, so its done row reached main ahead of its code while the landing was still refused) is replaced by LANDING=
decisions.why: Removes a route whose outcome was wrong (a settled row on main naming code not yet there) in favor of one that carries row and code together; nothing in request.md or the cited requirements asks for ENGINE=1, so its replacement narrows nothing the GM asked.

decisions.summary: fix_hold's message and the on-main refusal name the LANDING= route
decisions.why: The project's guard rule that a refusal names the compliant command (FR-012's form); serves the route.

decisions.summary: Filed as performance work; ordered after T179 (same arbiter crate) and lands beside it; exits on make crate-checks over reviews, task, land and arbiter crates with cover at 100%
decisions.why: FR-013 names work that makes the landings faster as performance work; the order and exits are scheduling and verification of the task's own behavior, not a narrowing.
